newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dlr on the mend as support surprises.
newsitem.headline: Australian dlr on the mend as support surprises.

text.p: The Australian dollar finished a consolidative Friday session near the week's highs after a startling offshore rally kept its recovery intact.

The currency had been in full retreat Thursday after dire domestic jobs data raised the ghost of another rate cut but overnight a combination of Swiss, U.S. and options-related bids came to the rescue. These were enough to recapture US$0.7820 and force stop-loss buying from those betting on weakness.
The bounce was eventually capped by fresh offers at US$0.7880, but dealers were impressed enough by the resilience of support to predict a test of US$0.7900 resistance next week.
By 5.00 pm (0700 GMT) the currency was making itself at home at US$0.7857/62 having rallied from an offshore low of US$0.7774 overnight and US$0.7800/05 late here Thuesday.

Analysts felt the performance a bullish one given the currency had delved as deep as US$0.7735 on Tuesday as market sentiment grew increasingly negative over the prospect of diminishing U.S./Australian interest rate differentials.

"What's surprised is that investors, particularly in Japan and Europe, have looked past the threat of closer official rates and bought Aussie bonds regardless," said one at a Melbourne based bank. "The demand's there and you can't argue with that."
The trail of that demand could be found on the crosses where the local dollar was up at 99.12/22 yen compared to 98.05/15 late Thursday and just 95.82/92 this time last week.
Before yesterday's lapse it had touched a five year high around 99.80, and analysts tipped a test of the psychologically important 100.00 barrier for the first time since May 1992.
Similarly it climbed sharply on the low yielding European currencies and stood at 1.3516/32 marks by the close from 1.3438/52 Thursday and only 1.3078/94 a week ago.
In trade weighted terms the broad-based strength lifted the index to 60.8 from 60.6 Thursday and 59.7 a week earlier.
Support was now expected at US$0.7820 and US$0.7775 and it would take a break of US$0.7735 to revive the former downtrend.

Analysts were surprised the prospect of a further narrowing US$/A$ interest differentials had not pressured the dollar more, but cautioned that if the Federal Reserve did hike at its May 20 meeting the reality was likely to take its toll on the A$.
There were key U.S. producer price and retail sales data out later today and could restrain the local currency if they add to the case for another tightening there.
The risk of a domestic easing still lay in the background despite bulls' efforts to explain away the weak March jobs data.
Analysts cautioned that housing finance figures out on Monday could well show a sharp fall in mortgage commitments if private banking data were anything to go by.
Some were looking for a drop of 10 percent or more ending two months of solid gains, an outcome which was likely to add further fuel to the easing fire.
Near term, however, many felt the outlook for low inflation here should keep real Australian yields attractive to offshore investors and underpin the currency.
